question.problem:
Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(4-3x).$

$\operatorname{ln}⁡(4-3x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯$
question.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4-3x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4(1-\frac{3x}{4})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{3x}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

The Maclaurin series for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-\frac{3x}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{3x}{4}) & =(-\frac{3x}{4})-\frac{1}{2}{(-\frac{3x}{4})}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(-\frac{3x}{4})}^{3}-⋯ \\  & =-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9{x}^{2}}{16})+\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{27{x}^{3}}{64})-⋯ \\  & =-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{32}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the desired result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4-3x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{3x}{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+(-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{32}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\frac{3x}{4}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{32}-\frac{9{x}^{3}}{64}-⋯\end{aligned}
$$
